items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: Of course, I had heard of him and... I had never heard him play in person then, but I knew who he was

ctx.x: get there early and run over the piano or whatever. So we got in, and I was playing over this piano. And one of the stagehands from the conservatory said, "Do you know whose piano that is you're playing?" I said "No." I thought it was a piano that belonged to the hall." He said, "That piano also belonged to Vladimir Horowitz. He had a concert here this afternoon." Of course, I had heard of him and... I had never heard him play in person then, but I knew who he was, and I was very honored and proud to be playing…

We finished I think it was a week at this club in Boston, and then we played that concert. After that, our next engagement was the Apollo Theatre in New York. I think we had about a week off when we got to New York, to rehearse, and we got new uniforms and the whole thing. By this time the band has got a good repertoire, and we're sounding pretty tight, and the whole thing is just about like we wanted it to be.
